saffra.name: Saffra Vell, Keeper of the Courtyard

umbra.name: Lady Umbra of the Black Kiln

acts.title: Wet Clay
acts.blurb: An apprentice at the town atelier. Learn the kilns, the racks and the mosaic.

acts.title: The Guild Kilns
acts.blurb: Glaziers of the guild test you: columns, prism tiles and a master's head start.

acts.title: The Sun Palace
acts.blurb: The palace mosaic goes to the best glazier alive. The Black Kiln wants it too.

twists.how: After newGame(), set G.first and G.cur to the boss seat so the boss holds the Sun token and makes the first take of round 1.
After newGame(), set the boss seat's score to param (P(boss).score = param) before the first take; the param is shown on the boss card.
After newGame(), for rows 1..param pull one Cobalt tile out of G.bag and set it on the boss mosaic at wall[r][WALLCOL(0,r)] (the Cobalt diagonal, legal on both mosaics).
In finish(), right after endBonus(), add param extra points to the boss for each complete mosaic column, logged as its own 'Boss rule' line.
While the chapter runs, set LVL.hard.roll = param and LVL.hard.K = 14 so the boss rolls out more futures per take, and restore {K:10, roll:2} on exit.

intro.text: Welcome to the atelier, apprentice. Five kilns, five glazes, one mosaic each.
On your turn, take every tile of ONE glaze from one kiln. The rest slides to the courtyard.
I'm new too! Let's just fill some racks and see what happens.

outro.text: Every full rack set one tile on your mosaic. That is the whole heartbeat of the craft.

opponent.name: Tamsin Reed
opponent.personality: Cheerful fellow apprentice who grabs the biggest pile she sees and often slips.

stars.text: Lose 6 or fewer points to breakage

easier.text: Tamsin slows down; the coach suggests every take.

intro.text: A lone tile on the mosaic scores 1. A tile touching others scores the whole line it joins.
Build your tiles next to each other, in rows and down columns.
I stoke the kilns all day. Scoring? I just set tiles wherever they land.

outro.text: See how the points grew as your tiles joined up? Neighbours pay.

opponent.name: Bram Kettle
opponent.personality: Big-handed kiln stoker; takes the largest pile and ignores where it goes.

easier.text: Bram plays gently and the coach points out the best space.

intro.text: Tiles that do not fit your racks fall to the breakage line, and each one costs points.
The Sun token is mine, child. I start every round, and you clean up my leftovers.
Take only what fits. A small take is often better than a big spill.

outro.text: Hm. You waste nothing. The guild will want to see you.
Pack your brushes. The guild kilns are next.

opponent.name: Saffra Vell
opponent.personality: Proud keeper of the courtyard; loves the Sun token and the first pick.
opponent.taunt: The courtyard always favours the one who holds the sun.
opponent.praise: Fine. Keep the courtyard tidy for me, glazier.

twist.text: Boss rule: Saffra holds the Sun token and makes the first take of round 1.

goal.text: Win, losing no more than 8 points to breakage.

stars.text: Win with 8 or fewer breakage points
Lose 3 or fewer points to breakage

easier.text: The boss rule is off: the Sun token starts at random.

intro.text: Guild rules, apprentice: a full column at the end is worth 7. A row only 2.
The game ends when someone finishes a row. Build down, not across, if you can.
I sort tiles all day. I also keep an eye on what YOU need.

outro.text: Seven for a column. You were listening.

opponent.name: Cobb the Sorter
opponent.personality: Careful guild sorter; weighs his gain against what he leaves you.

intro.text: Prism tiles are wild: they join any glaze on a rack. I already set one on my mosaic.
Take prisms with a glaze to finish a rack early. But a prism never counts for a full glaze.

outro.text: You bend the light better than I thought. Take this prism as a keepsake.

opponent.name: Iris Prismwright
opponent.personality: Dreamy glass artist; hoards prisms and finishes racks in one go.

twist.text: Rival rule: Iris starts with one Cobalt tile already set in mosaic row 1.

stars.text: Lose 4 or fewer points to breakage

easier.text: Iris plays gently and starts with an empty mosaic.

intro.text: I have glazed for forty summers. I will give you a contest, not a lesson.
And I begin with points in hand. The guild calls it respect.
Then out-build him. Columns and full glazes pay at the end; he can't hold them all.

outro.text: Forty summers, and an apprentice beats me fairly. The palace needs you.
A letter came, sealed in black. Someone else wants the Sun Palace mosaic.

opponent.name: Master Garnet Hale
opponent.personality: Stern guild master; never wastes a tile and starves your best racks.
opponent.taunt: Respect the head start, apprentice. Forty summers are hard to catch.
opponent.praise: You caught me. Take my seal to the palace gates.

twist.text: Boss rule: Master Garnet starts the game with 6 points.

stars.text: Earn a full glaze bonus (all 5 of one colour)

easier.text: Garnet plays gently and starts at 0 points.

intro.text: The palace gate is mine to guard. Only glaziers who think ahead get through.
Nell reads several turns ahead. Watch what your take leaves in the courtyard.

outro.text: Clean work. The gate is open; mind the halls.

opponent.name: Nell Frost
opponent.personality: Cool, patient gatekeeper; plays out the rest of the round before every take.

easier.text: Nell looks only one take ahead.

intro.text: Two of us, one of you. Three mosaics, seven kilns, and the courtyard fills fast.
With three at the table, the tile you skip may never come back. Plan for it.

outro.text: Both of us beaten! We'll tell the halls about you.

opponent.name: The Lumen Twins
opponent.personality: Two playful lamp-lighters who each chase their own mosaic, hard and fast.

easier.text: Only one twin plays, at normal strength.

intro.text: This wall has no painted colours. You choose each space, so no glaze repeats in a row or column.
And my columns are blessed by the Black Kiln. Each one pays me extra.
Vesper serves Lady Umbra. Finish the game before his columns fill.

outro.text: My lady will not be pleased. She waits in the throne hall.

opponent.name: Vesper Ash
opponent.personality: Quiet, precise servant of the Black Kiln; builds columns and nothing else.

twist.text: Rival rule: Vesper scores 3 extra points for each complete column at the end.

easier.text: Vesper plays at normal strength with no column blessing.

intro.text: The Sun Palace mosaic will be glazed in black. My kiln sees every future.
I play each take out to the end of the round, again and again. You only guess.
She weighs every pile. Give her none worth taking, and keep your breakage clean.

outro.text: The sun... in my own kiln. Very well. Glaze your palace.
The mosaic is yours, master glazier. The whole town will see it at noon.

opponent.name: Lady Umbra
opponent.personality: Cold mistress of the Black Kiln; deepest look-ahead, denies your best glaze.
opponent.taunt: Black glaze sets forever. Come back when you can see further.
opponent.praise: You out-saw the Black Kiln. The palace is yours, Sun Glazier.

twist.text: Boss rule: Lady Umbra studies twice as many futures before every take.

easier.text: Lady Umbra plays at normal strength and her deep sight is off.
